newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Union Pacific to move headquarters, cut staff.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific to move headquarters, cut staff.

text.p: Union Pacific Corp., still adjusting to recent acquisitions, said Tuesday that it will move its headquarters to either Texas or Missouri and cut more than 60 percent of its headquarters staff.

Chairman Dick Davidson said the relocation and staff cuts were necessary following the company's recent mergers with the Southern Pacific and Chicago and Northwestern railroads and the spin-off of its Union Pacific Resources Group Inc.
He said the company will cut the number of headquarters employees to about 45 from 120. Employees affected were offered either jobs in Omaha, Neb., or severance packages.
The company said it would move its headquarters from Bethlehem, Pa., to either Dallas/Ft. Worth, Texas, or St. Louis, Mo., two of its main operating areas.

Davidson said the company had determined after a review that many of the corporate functions would be managed more efficiently by integrating them. He added that he hoped to have the consolidation and relocation completed by September.
Union Pacific's recent mergers turned it into the nation's largest rail system with 36,000 miles of track in 23 western and midwestern states.
The company also operates Overnite Transporation Co., a Richmond, Va.-based trucking company, and Skyway Freight Systems, a Wattsonville, Calif.-based logistics and expedited transporation company.
Union Pacific's stock rose 37.5 cents to $60.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in midday trading.
